Topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle

Target audience: University students (CS/Math background) or curious tech enthusiasts

Section: section_1 — The Intuition: Why some guesses are 'better'

Lecture lines:
Wordle is a search problem for secret words.
A great guess narrows search space quickly.
Information gain measures how much we learn.

Planned animations:
Fade in a 'Wordle' grid at #FFFFFF with title 'The Intuition'. Wait 4s.
Display 'Guess' and 'Feedback' labels in #FFFF00. Wait 4s.
Show a 'Better Guess' icon (Green Star) at coordinate (-2, 0). Wait 4s.

Section: section_2 — Defining Information: The 'Surprise' Factor

Lecture lines:
Rare outcomes surprise us, providing more information.
Information is the negative log of probability.
Frequent events carry very little surprise value.

Planned animations:
Show 'Event X' icon in #00FFFF. Wait 4s.
Morph 'Event X' into 'Information Content' formula: I(x) = -log2(P(x)) in #FFFFFF. Wait 4s.
Scale 'I(x)' formula up to emphasize the surprise impact. Wait 4s.

Section: section_3 — Calculating Entropy: The Expected Information Gain

Lecture lines:
Entropy calculates the average information in guesses.
Guessing splits possibilities into equal-sized buckets.
High entropy choices resolve uncertainty fastest.
We average information gain across all outcomes.
Formula sums probability times surprise for all.

Planned animations:
Display 'Probability Distribution' histogram in #FF00FF. Wait 4s.
Overlay 'Entropy' summation formula: H(X) = Σ P(x)I(x) in #FFFFFF. Wait 4s.
Highlight each bar of the histogram sequentially as its P(x)I(x) contribution is added to H(X). Wait 4s.
Place a 'Goal Anchor' (Green Target SVG) at the final H(X) value. Wait 4s.
Pulse the 'Goal Anchor' to signify optimal balance. Wait 4s.

Section: section_4 — The Strategy: Maximizing Entropy

Lecture lines:
Algorithms don't search for the secret word.
They prioritize the most informative guess instead.
The bot tames uncertainty using entropy metrics.
Every outcome distribution is analyzed for gain.
Entropy maximization is the key strategy here.

Planned animations:
Show an 'Entropy Maximizer' slider in #00FF00. Wait 4s.
Visualize the slider moving to align with the 'Maximum Uncertainty' peak. Wait 4s.
Display 'Entropy H(X)' graph changing as the guess distribution shifts. Wait 4s.
Place a 'Terminal Target' icon on the highest point of the entropy curve. Wait 4s.
Highlight the final chosen guess distribution in bold yellow #FFFF00. Wait 4s.

Section: section_5 — Wrap-up: From Wordle to Reality

Lecture lines:
Entropy helps us compress data efficiently.
Medical diagnosis uses these principles to narrow tests.
This information theory applies everywhere in life.

Planned animations:
Display a 'World Map' icon to represent broader applications. Wait 4s.
Show 'Data Compression' and 'Decision Trees' text labels in #FFFFFF. Wait 4s.
Fade in 'Summary Conclusion' text to close the video. Wait 4s.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
